name: Early-onset Parkinsonism-Intellectual Disability Syndrome

criteria.description: Onset of parkinsonian motor symptoms before age 30
Presence of intellectual disability ranging from mild to severe
Exclusion of secondary causes of parkinsonism and intellectual disability by clinical and laboratory evaluation
Identification of pathogenic variants in causative genes (e.g., PTRHD1 mutations)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early-onset parkinsonism and intellectual disability with exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic causes of parkinsonism
imaging: Brain MRI may show nonspecific changes or mild cerebral atrophy
DAT-SPECT imaging showing reduced dopamine transporter uptake in basal ganglia
other: Clinical response to dopaminergic therapy variable and often limited

distinguishingFeatures: Often associated with PARK2 gene mutations
Characterized by infantile spasms and developmental regression
Prominent visual hallucinations and fluctuating cognition

redFlags: Early severe cognitive decline beyond baseline intellectual disability
Poor or no response to dopaminergic therapy
references: Orphanet: Early-onset parkinsonism-intellectual disability syndrome - ORPHA:2379
Klebe S, et al. PTRHD1 mutations cause autosomal recessive early-onset parkinsonism with intellectual disability. Brain. 2018.
